title: Composite & Custom Domain Types
description: Create reusable object types (CREATE TYPE ... AS), domain constraints with validation rules, and custom enums.

data.text: PostgreSQL's object-relational heritage enables developers to create custom composite types (structures containing multiple named attributes) and domains (scalar types with built-in validation constraints).

data.title: Creating a Validated Domain and Composite Type
data.content: Enforcing valid email format at the type level.

data.text: A **domain** is a base type plus optional `NOT NULL`, `DEFAULT`, and `CHECK` rules. The rule lives in one place and applies to every column declared with that domain — so a new table cannot forget the validation.

data.title: Domains That Encode Business Rules

data.text: Composite Types: Modelling a Value, Not a Row

A composite type is a named record. It is most useful for returning several values from a function and for storing a small, stable structure inside a column. It is *not* a substitute for a child table when the structure can repeat.

data.title: Composites Are Not Row Inheritance
data.text: A composite value inside a column cannot be joined, indexed field-by-field without an expression index, or constrained per field. If the structure is queried independently, use a child table. Reach for composite types for function return values and genuinely embedded values.

items.question: What is the difference between a domain, a composite type, and an enum?
items.answer: A domain constrains a scalar type; a composite type groups named fields into one value; an enum is a closed set of labelled scalar values. All three are created with `CREATE ... ` but they solve different problems.

items.question: Do domains hurt performance?
items.answer: No. A domain is the underlying type plus a check that runs on write — the same cost as a per-column `CHECK` constraint, but defined once.

items.question: Can I index a field inside a composite column?
items.answer: Yes, with an expression index: `CREATE INDEX ON clients (((shipping).country));`. The double parentheses are required because the inner parentheses are part of the field access.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Domains allow attaching reusable `CHECK` constraints to base types.
Composite types group attributes into cohesive objects.
Custom types provide strong architectural reuse across multiple tables.
